ow8_pipeline.topic: The weapons pipeline: FMS, notification, emergencies, co-production, Leahy, NSM-20

claims.text: FMS steps: pre-LOR consultation; Letter of Request to DoD implementing agency; case development and draft LOA; DSCA review coordinated with State (PM/RSAT approves); LOA cannot issue until statutory congressional review periods expire; partner signs and deposits into FMS Trust Fund; IA receives obligational authority, awards contracts or requisitions from DoD stock; delivery and Golden Sentry end-use monitoring; closure. DCS: foreign governments buy directly from US companies. FY2025 FMS system $104.4bn, $17.9bn FMF-funded; Israel among largest proposed sales.

AECA 36(b) thresholds: standard $14m MDE / $50m articles / $200m construction, 30 days; NATO, Japan, Australia, South Korea, Israel, New Zealand $25m / $100m / $300m, 15 days. Informal tiered review 20–40 days since 2012. Emergency: President states 'an emergency exists' requiring immediate sale, with detailed justification. Joint resolution of disapproval needs two-thirds to override a veto; Congress has never blocked a sale this way. DCS 36(c) same thresholds.

8–9 Dec 2023: Blinken determined 'an emergency exists' for 13,981 120mm tank cartridges, $106.5m, bypassing congressional review; such determinations rare, used by at least four administrations since 1979. 29 Dec 2023: second emergency sale, $147.5m: 4,792 M107 and 52,229 M795 155mm rounds and 30,000 M4 charges from US Army stock.

Late Feb–1 Mar 2025: Rubio waived congressional review to fast-track about $3bn in sales incl heavy bombs and armored bulldozers, and signed a declaration to expedite ~$4bn in military assistance, calling Biden's policy a 'partial arms embargo'; nearly $12bn in FMS approved since 20 Jan 2025.

May 2024 the US paused a shipment of 1,800 2,000-lb and 1,700 500-lb bombs over concern about a Rafah ground operation; Biden: 'Civilians have been killed in Gaza as a consequence of those bombs.' Trump released the 2,000-lb bombs on 25 Jan 2025.

Iron Dome US funding: FY2011 $205m; FY2012 $70m; FY2013 $194m; FY2014 $235.3m; FY2014 supplemental $225m; total $929.3m by FY2014. March 2014 coproduction agreement allowed US manufacture of components and gave MDA full access to Iron Dome technology; Raytheon Rafael's US partner; Sept 2014 $149m Raytheon parts contract.
23 Sep 2021 House passed $1bn Iron Dome replenishment 420–9 as stand-alone bill after removal from stopgap; DeLauro: 'entirely defensive'.
2016: US production funding for David's Sling (Rafael–Raytheon) and Arrow 3 (IAI–Boeing) split 50/50 with US partners; FY2017 appropriators: Iron Dome $62m, David's Sling $266.5m.

9 Oct 2026: R2S (Raytheon–Rafael JV) delivered first Tamir interceptors built in Camden, Arkansas, first facility outside Israel; plans US variant for Marine Corps MRIC. Marines tested MRIC with Tamir (SkyHunter in US service) at White Sands 30 Jun 2022.

Leahy laws: 22 USC 2378d (State) and 10 USC 362 (DoD) bar assistance to units with credible information of gross violations (torture, extrajudicial killing, enforced disappearance, rape under color of law); remediation exceptions; CRS notes reports that Israel's process differs.

Blaha (former director of State's Leahy vetting office, retired 2023): Israel Leahy Vetting Forum first met 2020; ineligibility decided by Deputy Secretary of State, 'true for no other country'; formal written requests to Israel first, up to three months; 'there are no ineligible Israeli units'; Blinken found four units remediated and Netzah Yehuda remained eligible. 9 Aug 2024 State said Netzah Yehuda 'effectively remediated'; Blaha called it 'directly contrary to the Leahy law'. Blaha is a senior adviser to DAWN.

NSM-20 issued 8 Feb 2024 from Van Hollen's Dec 2023 amendment: 'credible and reliable written assurances' on international law and to 'facilitate and not arbitrarily deny' humanitarian aid; 45 days for countries at war; report in 90 days. 10 May 2024 report: 'reasonable to assess' US arms used 'in instances inconsistent with its IHL obligations', no specific findings; Israel had not shared complete information; assurances 'credible and reliable'; no violation of FAA 620I. NSM-20 revoked 21 Feb 2025; NSM-18 CAT policy rescinded 14 Mar 2025, no explanation offered.
Of 85 FMS cases notified to Congress worldwide in 2023, the two December 2023 Israel sales were the only emergency invocations.
